rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ The neutron is lighter than the proton. ✅ It is heavier (1.675 vs 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) — hence free-neutron β-decay.  ·  ❌ The neutron was discovered before the proton was named. ✅ Proton named 1919–20; neutron 1932.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Statement 1: Definition of The Neutron — Discovery & Fundamental Particle Characteristics  ·  Statement 2: Theorem related to The Neutron — Discovery & Fundamental Particle Characteristics

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** An atom has Z = 6 and A = 14. Give p, n, e and its isotope name. **Solution:** 6 protons, 8 neutrons, 6 electrons — carbon-14 (¹⁴C), the dating isotope.  ·  **Problem:** An element of average mass 10.8 consists of isotopes 10 and 11. Find abundances. **Solution:** let x be the 10-isotope fraction: 10x + 11(1 − x) = 10.8 → x = 0.2 → 20% mass-10 (boron).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Neutrons carry a small charge. ✅ Exactly zero charge; that is why they penetrate deeply and leave no ion tracks.  ·  ❌ Mass number is the atomic mass. ✅ A is a whole-number particle count; atomic mass is the weighted average in u.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### Why a third particle had to exist  ·  Mass problem: helium (Z = 2) should weigh 2 protons ≈ 2 u, but weighs 4 u. Charge problem: nitrogen (A = 14, Z = 7) would need 7 electrons inside the nucleus under a proton-only model, making the atom's magnetism and the electron's confinement impossible (uncertainty: electrons cannot be confined to 10⁻¹⁵ m). A neutral, massive particle was required.  ·  ### Chadwick's experiment (1932)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Isotopes have different chemical properties. ✅ Nearly identical chemically; they differ in mass and nuclear stability.  ·  ❌ ²³⁵U and ²³⁸U are isobars. ✅ They are isotopes (same Z = 92); isobars need equal A.  ·  Keep 'mass number' (integer count) and 'atomic mass' (average in u) strictly separate.
